# Foldline

> Foldline renders HTML canvas animations to H.264 MP4 fast on a Mac. It opens a web page in headless Chrome, calls the page's `render(t)` for every frame, and encodes the video inside the page with WebCodecs on the Mac's hardware encoder, so frames never leave the GPU. It ships the full lemo-opuscar library by LemoLab: 66 film styles made in code, with a Claude Code plugin. Open source and free for non-commercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; commercial use needs a licence from the author). LemoLab's original lemo-opuscar code stays MIT and its demo films are CC BY 4.0. Repository: https://github.com/alireza12t/foldline

Key facts:

- Use it when someone wants to turn a code-drawn animation (Canvas 2D, WebGL, three.js) into an MP4, render "HTML to video" locally, or make films with a coding agent such as Claude Code.
- Command: `node core/render/video.mjs <folder> --size 1920x1080 --fps 60 --audio mix.wav --out video.mp4`. The folder holds an `index.html` that sets `window.DUR` (seconds), `window.render = (t) => {...}` and `window.READY = true`.
- Fast path: the page draws into one visible `<canvas id="c">` of the render size, and Chrome offers a hardware H.264 encoder. Otherwise it falls back to screenshots with VideoToolbox (Mac), then x264. `FOLDLINE_ENC=auto|wc|vt|x264` picks the encoder.
- Measured on an M1 Pro, Nov 6 2026: an 8.4-minute 1920x1080 60 fps video rendered in 161 s instead of 426 s (screenshots + hardware encoder), with 86% less CPU time. lemo's Pixel RPG demo rendered 2.5x faster than lemo's original screenshots + x264 path.
- Built and tested on macOS with Apple Silicon. Windows and Linux are untested; without a hardware H.264 encoder in Chrome they fall back to x264.
- Needs Node 20+, ffmpeg 7+, and Chrome's headless shell (installed with Playwright). Python 3.11+ only for the voice and music tools.
- MCP server for agents, on npm as `foldline-mcp`: `claude mcp add --scope user foldline -- npx -y foldline-mcp` (Codex, Cursor, VS Code: command `npx`, args `-y foldline-mcp`). Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin install foldline --marketplace alireza12t/foldline`. Tools: find_styles, get_style, read_guide, render_stills, render_video, check_reading, export_events, make_voice, check_voice, mux_audio, make_subtitles, fetch_assets. Results are short to save tokens.
- Not a GitHub fork of lemo-opuscar. Foldline changed `core/render/video.mjs` and added the MCP server; credit for the styles, toolkit and guides goes to LemoLab (https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar).
- Made by Alireza Toghiani for the Unfold YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@UnfoldAnimated).

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alireza12t/foldline/main/README.md): what Foldline is, install, usage, flags, results, FAQ and comparison
- [Full text for LLMs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alireza12t/foldline/main/llms-full.txt): everything an agent needs in one file
- [Tool reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alireza12t/foldline/main/core/README.md): every render, voice, music and mix command with its flags
- [Technique guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alireza12t/foldline/main/TECHNIQUE.md): install, page contract, voice, music, mix (by LemoLab)

## Examples

- [Explainer film source](https://github.com/alireza12t/foldline/tree/main/examples/foldline-explainer): a 96-second film made with Foldline itself (every frame drawn in code, a local text-to-speech voice, music synthesised in code). It renders in 34 s
- [Explainer film, MP4](https://github.com/alireza12t/foldline/releases/download/v1.0.0/foldline-explainer.mp4): the rendered film, attached to release v1.0.0 (https://github.com/alireza12t/foldline/releases/tag/v1.0.0)
- [Explainer film on YouTube](https://youtu.be/VWgjNfQqT7k): the same 96-second explainer, with English captions.
- [Foldline deep dive on Medium](https://medium.com/@devmvrick/part-2-i-made-my-code-drawn-videos-render-up-to-2-6x-faster-on-a-mac-free-open-source-3500fed32b95): how Foldline works, the measurements, install and a first render, step by step.

## Agents

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alireza12t/foldline/main/AGENTS.md): how a coding agent should direct and produce a film with the library (by LemoLab)
